audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL and CL logic including: Pectra fork activation (EIP-7600), provider event interfaces (EIP-2700), Phase 0 beacon chain state transitions and fork choice, Capella light client P2P, DELEGATECALL (EIP-7), KZG point evaluation precompile, CLZ opcode (EIP-7939), Cancun fork state transitions, EXP repricing (EIP-160), and bitwise shift instructions (EIP-145).

in_scope: EVM Execution (DELEGATECALL, EXP, SHL/SHR/SAR, CLZ opcodes)

el_attack_vectors.threat: Submit malformed transactions, exploit EXP underpricing for DoS, abuse DELEGATECALL to untrusted code, submit invalid KZG proof inputs
Send invalid blocks, propagate malformed transactions, eclipse attacks
Exploit DELEGATECALL context preservation to corrupt caller storage, submit crafted KZG proof inputs to point evaluation precompile, abuse shift opcodes for gas manipulation

cl_attack_vectors.entry_point: P2P Network (Beacon gossip, block proposals, attestations)
cl_attack_vectors.threat: Propose invalid blocks, submit conflicting attestations, equivocate to exploit fork choice, manipulate RANDAO
Request excessive bootstrap/update data for DoS, inject fake finality or optimistic updates via gossip
Provide incorrect finality data, feed false light client updates

misclassified_entities.reason: EIP-2700 models a browser-level provider interface (DApp ↔ wallet), not a protocol-level Ethereum node interface. The client application is a DApp interacting with a wallet extension, which is outside the EL/CL audit scope boundary. However, it represents a valid external entity at the wallet/provider trust boundary.

The wallet extension (EIP-2700) injects a provider into the page context. This is a browser-level trust boundary, not a protocol-level EL/CL boundary. Still modeled as it represents a valid external entity at the application trust boundary.

EIP-160 models the DoS attacker as an external entity. This is a threat actor, not a distinct system interface. The attacker's interaction is through standard channels (transaction submission), already covered by the User via JSON-RPC entity.
EIP-160 models the contract caller as external, but contract callers interact through standard transaction submission. Already covered by User via JSON-RPC for the EL boundary.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer (Validator) via P2P Gossip
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Beacon block proposals via P2P gossip (signed beacon blocks with execution payloads)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators propose blocks containing operations (attestations, slashings, deposits, exits). A malicious proposer can include invalid operations, attempt equivocation, or craft blocks to manipulate fork choice. All block content must be fully validated including header, RANDAO, state root, and all operations.

trusted_external_entities.name: Attesting Validator via P2P Gossip
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Indexed attestations via P2P gossip (fork choice on_attestation handler)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators submit attestations that influence fork choice head selection via LMD GHOST weight calculation. Malicious validators can submit conflicting attestations (equivocation), target incorrect checkpoints, or attempt balancing attacks. Attestation target, source, consistency, and equivocation status must be verified.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Network Peer via CL Gossip/Req-Resp
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: libp2p gossipsub and req/resp (beacon blocks, light client updates)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network peers deliver blocks to fork choice store (on_block handler) and light client protocol messages. Blocks must pass parent existence, slot timing, finalized descendant, and state transition checks. Light client messages require fork-version-aware SSZ deserialization validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Light Client Peer via P2P Gossip/Req-Resp
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Light client gossipsub topics and req/resp (GetLightClientBootstrap, LightClientUpdatesByRange, GetLightClientFinalityUpdate, GetLightClientOptimisticUpdate)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Light client peers request bootstrap data, update ranges, and finality/optimistic updates. Requests are unauthenticated. Malicious peers could attempt resource exhaustion via excessive requests. Responses must use correct fork-specific SSZ types and proper chunking across fork boundaries.

trusted_external_entities.name: ETH1 Deposit Contract via Merkle Proof
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Deposit operations in beacon blocks (Merkle proof against eth1_data.deposit_root)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The deposit contract is a deployed smart contract whose state is cryptographically verified via Merkle proofs. The contract itself is trusted (immutable code), but deposit data must be validated: Merkle proof verification, BLS signature check over DepositMessage. Invalid BLS signatures result in unusable validator records.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via devp2p
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers propagate blocks to the EL for state transition processing (Cancun fork). Blocks from peers must pass full validation: header consensus rules, body execution, Merkle root verification. Any peer can send invalid blocks.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users submit transactions including blob transactions (Cancun). Full validation required: nonce, balance, sender EOA check, fee structure, blob versioned hash format (KZG 0x01), blob gas limits. Covers all transaction types including type-3 blob transactions.

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Chain via Engine API (Withdrawals)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Engine API (withdrawal processing in block body)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The CL provides withdrawal data to the EL for balance crediting. Authenticated via JWT. Withdrawal amounts are converted to Wei and credited to recipients. The EL trusts the CL for withdrawal validity but must correctly apply state changes (balance increases, trie updates).

trusted_external_entities.name: Calling Contract via EVM CALL to Point Evaluation Precompile
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any contract can invoke the KZG point evaluation precompile with arbitrary input. Input must be exactly 192 bytes. Versioned hash, field elements (z, y < BLS_MODULUS), commitment, and proof must all be validated. The precompile must reject malformed inputs and invalid proofs. Fixed gas cost of 50000.

trusted_external_entities.name: Blob Data Source via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Blob data delivery via P2P (for KZG commitment verification)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network peers or local storage provide blob data alongside commitments and proofs for verification. Blob-specific verification derives evaluation challenges deterministically via Fiat-Shamir. Blob field elements must be < BLS_MODULUS. Invalid blobs must be rejected.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Beacon block processing (process_block: header, RANDAO, ETH1 data, operations)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Block must pass: correct slot > parent slot, correct parent root, correct proposer index, valid block signature, valid RANDAO reveal (BLS signature of epoch), valid ETH1 data vote, all operations validated (up to 16 proposer slashings, 2 attester slashings, 128 attestations, 16 deposits, 16 voluntary exits). State root must match after application.

Attestation target epoch must be current or previous epoch. Target root and beacon block root must be known in store. Target root must be consistent with checkpoint at target epoch. Equivocating validators (detected via on_attester_slashing) must be excluded from latest_messages updates.

Block must have known parent in store, slot not from future, must descend from finalized checkpoint. State transition must be applied and succeed. Timeliness recorded for proposer boost eligibility. Unrealized justified/finalized checkpoints updated.

Messages must be deserialized using correct fork-specific SSZ types. Nodes must reject messages from future forks they haven't activated. Light client finality and optimistic updates must be verified against sync committee signatures before acceptance.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Light client req/resp (GetLightClientBootstrap, LightClientUpdatesByRange, GetLightClientFinalityUpdate, GetLightClientOptimisticUpdate)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Responses must use fork-appropriate SSZ types. Range requests must be chunked by fork boundary. Rate limiting should be applied to prevent resource exhaustion from excessive requests.

Merkle proof must be verified against eth1_data.deposit_root. BLS signature over DepositMessage must be verified. Invalid BLS signatures result in validator record creation with unusable keys. Deposit count must match expected sequential index.

Full block validation: sequential block numbers, timestamp ordering, gas limit within parent±1/1024 and ≥5000, base fee calculation per EIP-1559, blob gas pricing, PoS field validation. Body execution with Merkle root verification (transactions, receipts, withdrawals, state). Reject InvalidBlock on any failure.

Nonce match, sufficient balance, sender is EOA, EIP-1559 fee structure valid. For blob txs: versioned hash version 0x01, blob gas within limits. Gas refund capped at 20% of consumed. Priority fee paid to proposer. Empty accounts cleaned up.

Withdrawal data from CL is trusted (JWT-authenticated channel). EL must correctly convert amounts to Wei (multiply by 10^9), increase recipient balances, and update withdrawal trie. Withdrawal root must match header value.

Input must be exactly 192 bytes. Versioned hash must start with 0x01. Field elements z and y must be < BLS_MODULUS. Commitment and proof must be valid G1 curve points. KZG proof verification must use trusted library. Fixed gas cost 50000. Output is FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB and BLS_MODULUS on success.

Blob field elements must be < BLS_MODULUS. Evaluation challenge derived deterministically via Fiat-Shamir (FSBLOBVERIFY_V1_ domain). Polynomial evaluated at challenge using barycentric interpolation. KZG proof verified via pairing check. Batch verification uses separate domain (RCKZGBATCH___V1_).

notes: EIP-7600 (Pectra fork activation), EIP-7 (DELEGATECALL), EIP-7939 (CLZ), and EIP-145 (bitwise shifts) have no external entities as they model internal EVM/consensus state transitions without external data ingress.
EIP-2700 external entities (EXT-CLIENT-APP, EXT-WALLET) are at the browser/wallet trust boundary, outside the core EL/CL protocol scope but noted in misclassified_entities.
EIP-160 entities (EXT-ATTACKER, EXT-CONTRACT-CALLER) are threat actors or generic callers subsumed by EXT-USER-JSON-RPC.
